title: AVL right rotation
summary: Rotate the first unbalanced node right. Rearrange the links within its subtree, then attach the new subtree root to its parent.
context: Root 4 has left child 3 and right child 5; 3 has only a left child, 1, and 1 only a left child, 0. Nodes 0 and 5 are leaves.

The balance factor is left subtree height minus right subtree height. Height is measured in edges: a leaf has height 0 and an empty subtree −1. Scanning upward, 3 is the first unbalanced node. Call it node and its left child 1 child.
description: Here the right subtree of child (1) is empty. The code first saves grand_child = child.right, then sets child.right = node and finally node.left = grand_child. The old reference must be saved before it is overwritten.
result: The subtree height decreases by 1. The entire tree regains AVL balance while preserving binary search tree order.

frames.title: Find the first unbalanced node, 3
frames.explanation: Root 4 has left child 3 and right child 5; 3 has only a left child, 1, and 1 only a left child, 0. Nodes 0 and 5 are leaves. The factors printed below nodes are 0 for nodes 0 and 5, 1 for node 1, and 2 for nodes 3 and 4. Moving up the left branch, 3 is the first unbalanced node, so repair its subtree first.
frames.key_state: Root 4 has left child 3 and right child 5; 3 has only a left child, 1, and 1 only a left child, 0. Nodes 3 and 4 both have factor 2. The bottom-up check handles 3 first.
frames.announcement: Check balance factors from the bottom up to locate the first unbalanced node, 3.

frames.title: Mark the two nodes involved in the rotation
frames.explanation: Mark node=3 and child=1 before rotating. Root 4 has left child 3 and right child 5; 3 has only a left child, 1, and 1 only a left child, 0. Since child.right is empty, the saved grand_child is empty and node.left must also be empty after rotation.
frames.key_state: Before rotation: Root 4 has left child 3 and right child 5; 3 has only a left child, 1, and 1 only a left child, 0. Here node=3, child=1, and child.right is empty.
frames.announcement: Mark the unbalanced subtree root node = 3 and its left child, child = 1.

frames.title: Form the local subtree rooted at 1
frames.explanation: Save the old right link of child (empty), then set child.right = node and node.left = grand_child. The new local root 1 has left leaf 0 and right leaf 3. For now parent 4 has only its right child 5; it has not yet reconnected to 1. The dashed outline at the old 3 and its dashed edge to 1 show the old layout, not current links. The full rotation is still in progress.
frames.key_state: Local root 1 has left child 0 and right child 3. Parent 4 has only right child 5 and is not yet linked to new root 1.
frames.announcement: Node 3 becomes the right child of 1. The new subtree exists but has not yet been linked back to parent 4.

frames.title: Reconnect the new subtree root to its parent
frames.explanation: Point 4.left to new subtree root 1. Root 4 now has left child 1 and right child 5; 1 has left child 0 and right child 3. Nodes 0, 3, and 5 are leaves. The subtree height falls by 1 and the balance factor at root 4 changes from 2 to 1. Inorder traversal still gives [0, 1, 3, 4, 5].
frames.key_state: After reconnection, root 4 has left child 1 and right child 5; 1 has left child 0 and right child 3. The inorder sequence is [0, 1, 3, 4, 5]. The entire tree is balanced.
frames.announcement: Point parent 4’s left link to new root 1, completing the right rotation and restoring balance throughout the tree.
